episode.throughLine: A rejected classical-piano applicant continues private study and paid teaching, loses studio work, and takes paid piano-and-singing work without having the school rejection reversed.

contentProfile.contentNote: Music-school rejection, remembered shame and self-doubt, Simone's attributed belief that racism caused her rejection, and loss of paid work. Short source-led vignette; accounts disagree about the first singing requirement, which is not staged. Ages 18–21 narrow installed 17–21.

arc.canonicalText: She was eighteen when she auditioned on the piano for a music school. She wanted to play classical music professionally. The school did not admit her.
arc.sourceNote: Short source-led vignette, not a fully located moment sequence. Later emotions are memory-framed and probable. No result-delivery medium, first lesson, room, body gesture or healing is invented. New prose requires owner reading; empty review is not approval.

arc.canonicalText: She remembered shame, anger and doubt about whether her playing was good enough. She believed racial prejudice had kept her out. The career she wanted remained out of reach.
arc.sourceNote: Short source-led vignette, not a fully located moment sequence. Later emotions are memory-framed and probable. No result-delivery medium, first lesson, room, body gesture or healing is invented. New prose requires owner reading; empty review is not approval.

arc.canonicalText: She continued studying privately with a teacher from the school that had refused her. She also taught piano and played for vocal students to earn money. She had lessons to pay for.
arc.sourceNote: Short source-led vignette, not a fully located moment sequence. Later emotions are memory-framed and probable. No result-delivery medium, first lesson, room, body gesture or healing is invented. New prose requires owner reading; empty review is not approval.

arc.canonicalText: Three summers later, the vocal studio closed while its students went on holiday. The closure left her without that job. She was twenty-one.
arc.sourceNote: Short source-led vignette, not a fully located moment sequence. Later emotions are memory-framed and probable. No result-delivery medium, first lesson, room, body gesture or healing is invented. New prose requires owner reading; empty review is not approval.

arc.canonicalText: She took paid work at a bar, playing piano and singing. Singing was part of what the employer required. The job used both skills.
arc.sourceNote: The vignette states only the overlapping result of competing 1960/1969 accounts: paid piano/singing work with a singing requirement. No hiring conversation, first-night ultimatum, exact wage or first-ever singing is recreated. Estate biography and 1960 reporting support 1954; conflicting 1969 year remains disclosed.

arc.canonicalText: Her performances brought popular songs together with her classical piano training. She was earning through music outside the concert career she had wanted. The school had not changed its answer. She had a place to perform.
arc.sourceNote: Short source-led vignette, not a fully located moment sequence. Later emotions are memory-framed and probable. No result-delivery medium, first lesson, room, body gesture or healing is invented. New prose requires owner reading; empty review is not approval.

arc.canonicalText:
Her name was Nina Simone.

She became known as a singer and pianist.

Your life is not theirs. But a piece of this story may still sit beside you.

You do not have to turn disappointment into gratitude. You are allowed to miss what you wanted.

dramatizationLimits: No invented audition-room details, rejection letter, gesture or private thought.
Do not combine incompatible interview sequences.
No fabricated scenes for habitual lessons or teaching.
avoidRules: Never state racial discrimination or its absence as a proved jury motive.
Do not call her a Juilliard graduate or Curtis student.
Do not say the singing requirement caused her first-ever use of her voice.
No claim that she became the first Black classical pianist.
Do not settle the contested audition motive, hiring sequence or first-night date; the new vignette deliberately omits that sequence.
